ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν
θάλασσαν, καὶ γενήσεται οὕτως. οὐδήπου γὰρ ὡς πρὸς ἀπίστους τὴν κοινὴν πίστιν
ταῦτα πρὸς αὐτοὺς διελέγετο.

Fragmentum in epistulam ii ad Corinthios
2 Kor 10,7 Κατ' ἐπιτιμητικὴν ὑπόκρισιν τοῦτο ἀναγνωστέον· οὐκ ἐκ τῶν
ἔργων, ἀντὶ τοῦ τῆς ἀληθείας, τὴν ἐξέτασιν, ἐκ δὲ τῶν ἐπιπολῆς ἁπλῶς φαινομένων
λαμβάνετε.
thought_title: Faith as mustard seed and reproachful reading of 2 Corinthians 10:7
orientation: Gennadius is explaining Paul's mention of the spiritual gift of faith, and then comments on how to read 2 Corinthians 10:7.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning this also the Lord says in the Gospels: if you have faith as a grain of mustard, you will say to this mountain: be lifted up and be thrown into the sea, and it will happen thus. For nowhere as toward unbelievers was he discussing the common faith these things toward them. Fragment on the Second Epistle to the Corinthians. 2 Cor 10:7. This must be read with reproachful hypocrisy: not from the works, instead of from the truth, do you take the examination, but from the things appearing simply on the surface.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'hypocrisy' for this term, and the context is reproachful feigned speech.
It modifies 'hypocrisy' and conveys the censuring tone of the reading.
It contrasts with the truth of works, indicating outward appearances.
It renders the act of judging or scrutinizing that the Corinthians are doing wrongly.

bible_refs.note: ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν

pass_b_english: About this the Lord also says in the Gospels: “If you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and it will happen” (Matthew 17:20). For he was certainly not discussing the common faith with them as if they were unbelievers.
Fragment on the Second Epistle to the Corinthians
This must be read with reproachful hypocrisy: you take your examination not from works—that is, from the truth—but simply from what appears on the surface (2 Corinthians 10:7).
